reason: A fragment of 'distinct nearly to base' on bracts, bracteoles and tepals. The previous review mapped 'distinct' on such parts to FLOPO:0991068 free. 'Nearly to base' gives how far they are free, which can be kept in the record's source words.
The inflorescence (or fruiting spike) is fertile along its whole length. 'Throughout' gives the extent, as against 'only proximally', and is not a separate quality.

target: the described part (seed PO_0009010, offset PO_0005001, petal PO_0009032) present; 'not formed' = absent (docs/odp/15-absence-of-a-part.md)
reason: 'Seeds rarely formed' and 'offsets not formed' say whether the bearer itself comes into being. That is a presence or absence of the part, with a frequency.
A comparison with one genus whose meaning (thick, horizontal, fleshy?) is not fixed. The examples already state 'thick' separately, and two floras do not justify a term.

target: spirally arranged (FLOPO:0991114), as a quality of the inflorescence towards its flowers (docs/odp/16-quality-of-a-whole-towards-its-parts.md)
reason: Spikes 'loosely to tightly spiraled' (as in Spiranthes) have their flowers inserted along a spiral. 'Loosely' is a degree adverb and should stay in the source words.
A direct negation of the existing value class secund.
Negates PATO inflexible (exact synonym 'stiff'). A negation is more faithful than asserting PATO_0001544 flexible.
Cottony hair cover is PATO floccose (exact synonym 'cottony'). 'Cottony hairs absent' becomes the negation of the same quality.

The phrase names a kind of hair, and the statements give its density or absence. FLOPO:0991148 crisped is a margin shape and does not fit hairs, so the hair is the bearer and PATO curled is the qualifier.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) of the described organ + dark brown (PATO_0001245)
reason: The colour belongs to the veins, not to the petal or leaf. The record should have the vein as bearer, as part of the described organ, with the PATO colour.
A length-to-width ratio with a numeric range is a ratio of two dimensions of the same bearer.

target: acute (sensu botany) (FLOPO:0991095), bearer: apex (FLOPO_0985023) of the leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517)
reason: The phrase is a bearer (lobe apex) plus the existing botanical acute. It needs no new term.
'Multicellular-hairy' means bearing multicellular hairs. PO has the hair type, so this is a presence rule.
FLOPO trigonous is already defined as triangular in cross-section with rounded angles. 'Rounded-trigonous' and the Spanish 'redondeado-trígonos' state that definition.

target: docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md (equality of colour with petal PO_0009032)
reason: An equality of one quality (colour) with another part. The colour itself is not given, so the pattern records the comparison.
A length comparison of the pistillate scale with the perigynium, sometimes given as a fraction (pattern 10).
'Fruits silicles' names a fruit type, not a quality. PO has silicle as a synonym of silique fruit. The short-versus-long distinction is lost, but it can be stated through the length-to-width pattern.
Flakelike perispore projections are small, thin and flat, which is the definition of FLOPO scale-like.

label: semioblong
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being one half of an oblong figure divided lengthwise, with one side straight and the other running nearly parallel to it and rounded at the ends.
reason: Same series as the accepted FLOPO:0991318 semiovate and FLOPO:0991275 semi-elliptic. It is used for orchid lip lobes, bracts and calyx teeth.

label: shoot-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling an elongated leafy shoot, with an evident axis bearing spaced leaves, rather than a compact bud.
reason: Floras contrast shoot-like turions with compact, bud-like ones, so it is a real character state. It is the sibling of FLOPO:0991288 bud-like and FLOPO:0991359 stolon-like.
'Squarrulose' (slightly squarrose) describes spreading leaf or bract tips and makes no sense for a fruit surface. 'Squarrulose maculate' looks like a mistranslation of a spotting pattern.
'Unbent' phyllaries or laminae are not bent back, that is, straight.
'With two saccate pouches' is a count compound like '5-nerved', built on the existing saccate.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: flattened PATO_0002254 + square PATO_0000413)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two existing values. Both are asserted of the stigma, and no new term is needed.
Cowl-like means hood-shaped, which is the definition of FLOPO cucullate.
Branched is the quality. 'Irregularly' is not defined well enough for its own class and stays in the source words.

A fern venation term whose exact meaning I could not confirm from the repository files, from only six statements. Its nearest relative is FLOPO:0991339 catadromous, and it needs a check against a pteridological glossary before any term is made.
A typo for 'obtuse' on apices of leaves, sepals and ovaries.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: papillose FLOPO:0991059 + ciliated PATO_0001408)
reason: A compound of two margin values that already exist. It could also mean cilia that are short and papilla-like, which also argues against a single term.

label: forcipate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending in two arms or horns that curve towards each other like the jaws of pincers.
reason: A recognised botanical shape (forcipate) used for styles and for fruits with incurved apical horns. Existing classes such as horned or claw-shaped do not cover the paired incurved arms.
